headline: American Lung Association: Senate funding bills are 'a step in the right direction' but should go further on lung health
dek: The American Lung Association outlined how Senate appropriations bills treat CDC, EPA and NIH programmes relevant to lung health, ahead of a 11 December deadline for agreement with the House.
body:
The American Lung Association said on LinkedIn that the Senate has released appropriations bills that are "a step in the right direction" but "should go further to fund lung health programs".

The organisation said the bills maintain funding for several Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) programmes: the National Asthma Control Program, the Office of Smoking Health, the National Center on Environmental Health, and Chronic Disease Education and Awareness.

For the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the association described a slight cut to overall agency funding, along with decreases for clean air programmes and for pollution clean-up enforcement and compliance. It said funding stays the same for programmes that clean up diesel pollution and radon, and for air quality monitoring grants.

For the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the association said the bills increase funding by $500 million.

The association said Senate and House appropriators need to agree on funding levels by 11 December. It urged supporters to contact Congress to keep lung health a priority during the negotiations, and directed them to a text-message campaign and a web page for taking action.
key_quote: The Senate just put out appropriations bills that are a step in the right direction but should go further to fund lung health programs.
